name: TRANFILE.jcl
description:
This JCL job initializes and rebuilds the Transaction Master VSAM file structure for the CardDemo application. It deletes existing VSAM files, recreates the primary keyed cluster and alternate index, loads initial transaction data, and reopens the files for online CICS processing.Key Functionalities:
Closes the Transaction (TRANSACT) and Alternate Index (CXACAIX) CICS files before any structural changes to prevent data corruption during the rebuild process.
Deletes the existing Transaction VSAM KSDS cluster (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS) and its Alternate Index (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX), suppressing warnings for conditions up to return code 8 (e.g., file not found).
Recreates the Transaction VSAM KSDS cluster with a primary key of 16 bytes starting at offset 0, fixed record size of 350 bytes, allocated 1 primary cylinder with 5 secondary cylinders on volume AWSHJ1, with share options (2,3).
Loads initial transaction data from the sequential seed file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYTRAN.PS.INIT) into the newly created VSAM KSDS cluster.
Defines a new Alternate Index (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX) on the KSDS with a non-unique key of 26 bytes at offset 304, allocated 5 primary cylinders with 1 secondary cylinder, set to automatically upgrade when the base cluster is updated.
Creates an Access Path (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX.PATH) for the Alternate Index to enable access to the KSDS via the alternate key.
Builds the Alternate Index entries by scanning the base KSDS cluster and populating the AIX dataset.
Reopens the TRANSACT and CXACAIX CICS files to restore online transaction processing availability after the rebuild is complete.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo Transaction Master File rebuild job has been initiated AND the CICS region CICSAWSA is actively serving online users with access to the Transaction Primary File (TRANSACT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The batch job begins its pre-processing phase and issues a command to the CICSAWSA CICS region to close the TRANSACT file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The TRANSACT file in the CICSAWSA CICS region must be closed AND online users must no longer be able to access Transaction records via Transaction ID lookup through the CICS online interface until the file is explicitly reopened at the end of the rebuild process

rules.Rule_Name: CLCIFIL - SDSF - Close CICS Transaction Primary File Before Batch Rebuild
rules.Rule_Description: Before the Transaction Master File rebuild process begins, the CICS online Transaction Primary File (TRANSACT) must be closed in the CICSAWSA region to prevent simultaneous online and batch access, ensuring data integrity during the rebuild.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo Transaction Master File rebuild job has been initiated AND the CICS region CICSAWSA is actively serving online users with access to the Card Number Alternate Index File (CXACAIX)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The batch job begins its pre-processing phase and issues a command to the CICSAWSA CICS region to close the CXACAIX file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The CXACAIX file in the CICSAWSA CICS region must be closed AND online users must no longer be able to retrieve Transaction records by Card Number through the CICS online interface until the file is explicitly reopened at the end of the rebuild process

rules.Rule_Name: CLCIFIL - SDSF - Close CICS Card Number Alternate Index File Before Batch Rebuild
rules.Rule_Description: Before the Transaction Master File rebuild process begins, the CICS online Card Number Alternate Index File (CXACAIX) must be closed in the CICSAWSA region to prevent simultaneous online and batch access, ensuring data integrity during the rebuild.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Master File rebuild process has been initiated and the CICS Transaction files have already been closed for batch processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to delete the Transaction Primary Dataset (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS) including all its components (data and index)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the deletion completes successfully (return code = 0), the Transaction Primary Dataset is fully removed and processing continues to the next deletion; AND if the dataset does not exist (return code = 8), this is treated as a successful outcome (return code is reset to 0) and processing continues to the next deletion; AND if the deletion fails for any other reason (return code greater than 8, such as the dataset being in use, a security violation, or a system error), the step fails and the entire job stops with no further steps executed

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05 - IDCAMS - Delete Existing Transaction Primary Dataset Before Rebuild
rules.Rule_Description: Before rebuilding the Transaction Master File system from scratch, the existing Transaction Primary Dataset (KSDS) must be deleted. The process must tolerate the case where the dataset does not yet exist, treating it as a successful outcome so that the rebuild can safely proceed in both fresh and existing environments.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Primary Dataset deletion in the same step has completed successfully (or was found absent and treated as success), and the process is now proceeding to remove the Card Number Alternate Index
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to delete the Card Number Alternate Index (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX) which provides Card Number-based access to Transaction records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the deletion completes successfully (return code = 0), the Card Number Alternate Index is fully removed and the step completes successfully, allowing the job to proceed to dataset recreation; AND if the Alternate Index does not exist (return code = 8), this is treated as a successful outcome (return code is reset to 0) and the step completes successfully, allowing the job to proceed to dataset recreation; AND if the deletion fails for any other reason (return code greater than 8, such as the index being in use, a security violation, or a system error), the step fails and the entire job stops with no further steps executed, leaving the Transaction Master File system in an incomplete state

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05 - IDCAMS - Delete Existing Card Number Alternate Index Before Rebuild
rules.Rule_Description: As part of the Transaction Master File rebuild, the existing Card Number Alternate Index must also be deleted after the Transaction Primary Dataset is removed. The process must equally tolerate the case where the Alternate Index does not yet exist, treating it as a successful outcome so that the rebuild can safely proceed in both fresh and existing environments.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new Transaction Master Dataset needs to be created for the CardDemo application
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Master Dataset is defined in the system
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The dataset must be created with the official name 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS', organized as an indexed (Key-Sequenced) dataset, with a dedicated Data component named 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS.DATA' and a dedicated Index component named 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS.INDEX'

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Define Transaction Master Dataset Identity
rules.Rule_Description: Establishes the official name and structural identity of the Transaction Master Dataset as a Key-Sequenced (indexed) data store within the CardDemo system, ensuring it is uniquely identifiable and organized for direct Transaction ID-based access.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Master Dataset is being defined with a primary key for record identification
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key structure of the Transaction Master Dataset is configured
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID must be defined as the primary key with a length of exactly 16 bytes, starting at the very first byte (position 0) of every Transaction record, ensuring every transaction is uniquely identifiable and directly retrievable by its Transaction ID

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Define Transaction Record Key Structure
rules.Rule_Description: Establishes the Transaction ID as the primary unique identifier for every Transaction record, defining its exact position and length within the record layout so that every transaction can be directly located and retrieved by its Transaction ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Master Dataset is being defined with a record size specification
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A Transaction record is stored in or retrieved from the Transaction Master Dataset
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Every Transaction record must be exactly 350 bytes in both minimum and maximum length (RECORDSIZE 350 350), meaning no variable-length records are permitted — all Transaction records must conform to the fixed 350-byte structure

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Enforce Fixed Transaction Record Size
rules.Rule_Description: Enforces that every Transaction record stored in the Transaction Master Dataset must be exactly 350 bytes in length — no shorter and no longer — ensuring uniform record structure across all transactions in the CardDemo system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Master Dataset requires physical disk storage allocation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Master Dataset is created on the system
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The dataset must be allocated on disk volume AWSHJ1 with an initial primary allocation of 1 cylinder, and must be permitted to automatically expand by up to 5 additional secondary cylinders when the primary allocation is exhausted, for a maximum total capacity of 6 cylinders

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Define Transaction Dataset Storage Allocation
rules.Rule_Description: Defines the initial and maximum storage capacity for the Transaction Master Dataset on a designated disk volume, ensuring sufficient space is reserved for Transaction data while allowing for controlled growth as transaction volume increases.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Master Dataset may be accessed by multiple batch jobs or systems simultaneously
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The concurrent access policy for the Transaction Master Dataset is configured
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The dataset must enforce Share Option 2 for cross-region access (multiple jobs within the same system may read simultaneously, but only one job may write at a time) and Share Option 3 for cross-system access (multiple systems may read or write simultaneously), as defined by SHAREOPTIONS(2 3)

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Enforce Concurrent Access Policy for Transaction Data
rules.Rule_Description: Defines the rules governing simultaneous access to the Transaction Master Dataset by multiple batch jobs and systems, protecting Transaction data integrity while allowing controlled concurrent read access across the CardDemo processing environment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Master Dataset contains sensitive financial transaction records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Master Dataset is deleted from the system at any point in the future
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All Transaction data stored in the dataset must be physically erased from the disk (ERASE attribute), ensuring that sensitive financial transaction information cannot be recovered or reconstructed by any means after deletion

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Enforce Transaction Data Security on Deletion
rules.Rule_Description: Enforces a data security policy requiring that all Transaction data is physically and permanently wiped from disk whenever the Transaction Master Dataset is deleted, preventing unauthorized recovery of sensitive financial transaction information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Daily Transaction Initialization flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYTRAN.PS.INIT) exists and contains Card Transaction records, AND the Transaction VSAM Primary Dataset (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS) has been freshly created and is empty, AND both datasets are available for shared access
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction record load process is triggered to populate the Transaction Master Dataset from the Daily Transaction Initialization file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Every Card Transaction record from the Daily Transaction Initialization flat file is copied in its entirety (all 350 bytes per record) into the Transaction VSAM Primary Dataset, AND all copied Transaction records are automatically organized and stored in ascending order by their Transaction ID (the unique 16-byte identifier at the start of each record), AND upon successful completion the Transaction VSAM Primary Dataset contains a complete and fully indexed copy of all initial daily Transaction records ready for both direct Transaction ID-based lookup and sequential browsing, AND if the load fails for any reason (such as a duplicate Transaction ID, source file unavailable, or insufficient storage space) the step fails and no further processing occurs leaving the Transaction dataset empty or incomplete and unusable

rules.Rule_Name: STEP15 - IDCAMS REPRO - Load Daily Transaction Records into Transaction Master Dataset
rules.Rule_Description: This step loads all Card Transaction records from the Daily Transaction Initialization flat file into the Transaction VSAM Primary Dataset. All records are copied in full without filtering or transformation, and are automatically organized by Transaction ID upon entry into the VSAM dataset. Both the source and target datasets are accessed in shared mode, allowing other processes to read them concurrently during the load.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Primary Dataset (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS) exists and contains Transaction records, and no Alternate Index named AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX currently exists
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card Number Alternate Index definition is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new Alternate Index named AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX must be created and formally associated with the Transaction Primary Dataset (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS) as its base cluster, establishing Card Number as a valid secondary access path to Transaction records

rules.Rule_Name: STEP20 - IDCAMS - Define Card Number Alternate Index Over Transaction Master Dataset
rules.Rule_Description: Define a secondary index structure over the Transaction Master Dataset that enables retrieval of Transaction records using Card Number as a lookup key, establishing the relationship between the Alternate Index and the Transaction Primary Dataset.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Each Transaction record in the Transaction Primary Dataset is exactly 350 bytes in fixed length
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Alternate Index key definition is applied
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card Number field — spanning 26 bytes starting at byte position 304 within each Transaction record — must be designated as the secondary lookup key for the Alternate Index, so that any search by Card Number uses exactly these 26 bytes at position 304 to locate matching Transaction records

rules.Rule_Name: STEP20 - IDCAMS - Define Card Number as Secondary Lookup Key for Transaction Records
rules.Rule_Description: Designate the Card Number field — located at a specific position within each Transaction record — as the secondary key for the Alternate Index, enabling Transaction records to be retrieved by Card Number in addition to Transaction ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Number Alternate Index is being defined over the Transaction Primary Dataset
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The NONUNIQUEKEY policy is applied to the Alternate Index
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Alternate Index must allow multiple Transaction records to share the same Card Number key value — meaning one Card Number can map to many Transaction IDs — and the index must store and return all Transaction records associated with a given Card Number when a Card Number-based lookup is performed

rules.Rule_Name: STEP20 - IDCAMS - Allow Multiple Transactions Per Card Number
rules.Rule_Description: Enforce the business rule that a single Credit Card Number can be associated with many Transaction records, reflecting the real-world relationship where one card generates multiple transactions over time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Number Alternate Index has been defined with the UPGRADE attribute over the Transaction Primary Dataset
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A Transaction record is added to or deleted from the Transaction Primary Dataset (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS) by any batch or online process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card Number Alternate Index (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX) must be automatically updated to reflect the change — new Card Number-to-Transaction-ID mappings must be added for inserted records, and existing mappings must be removed for deleted records — without requiring any separate manual index maintenance job

rules.Rule_Name: STEP20 - IDCAMS - Automatically Synchronize Card Number Index When Transaction Data Changes
rules.Rule_Description: Ensure the Card Number Alternate Index remains current and accurate at all times by automatically reflecting any additions or deletions of Transaction records in the Transaction Primary Dataset without requiring manual index maintenance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Number Alternate Index is being defined to mirror the structure of the Transaction Primary Dataset
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record size definition is applied to the Alternate Index
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Both the minimum and maximum record size of the Alternate Index must be set to exactly 350 bytes — no Alternate Index record may be shorter or longer than 350 bytes — ensuring structural consistency between the Alternate Index and the Transaction Primary Dataset

rules.Rule_Name: STEP20 - IDCAMS - Enforce Fixed Record Size for Card Number Alternate Index
rules.Rule_Description: Enforce that all records within the Card Number Alternate Index conform to a fixed length of 350 bytes, consistent with the Transaction Primary Dataset record structure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Number Alternate Index is being created for the first time on the mainframe storage environment
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The storage allocation definition is applied
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Alternate Index must be allocated on disk volume AWSHJ1 with a primary allocation of 5 cylinders and a secondary (overflow) allocation of 1 additional cylinder — the primary allocation of 5 cylinders must be reserved immediately upon creation, and the secondary cylinder must be automatically acquired if the index grows beyond the initial 5 cylinders

rules.Rule_Name: STEP20 - IDCAMS - Allocate Dedicated Storage for Card Number Alternate Index
rules.Rule_Description: Allocate sufficient and expandable disk storage for the Card Number Alternate Index on the designated storage volume to support the expected volume of Card Number-to-Transaction mappings.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Number Alternate Index (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX) is being defined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The component naming definition is applied
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Two distinct named components must be created: (1) a DATA component named AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX.DATA — which physically stores the Card Number-to-Transaction-ID mapping records — and (2) an INDEX component named AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX.INDEX — which stores the index structure used to navigate the data component — both components must be independently identifiable and manageable by their respective names

rules.Rule_Name: STEP20 - IDCAMS - Define Named Data and Index Components for Card Number Alternate Index
rules.Rule_Description: Establish uniquely named physical storage components for the Card Number Alternate Index — one for the actual index data records and one for the index structure — enabling independent management and identification of each component.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Number Alternate Index (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX) has been successfully defined in the previous step (STEP20) and exists on disk volume AWSHJ1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is requested to define a new named access path called AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX.PATH with its entry point set to the Card Number Alternate Index AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A permanent named logical access path AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX.PATH is successfully created and registered, linking application programs to the Card Number Alternate Index so that any program opening this path by name can retrieve all Transaction records associated with a given Credit Card Number; if the path definition fails for any reason (e.g., the Alternate Index does not exist, naming conflict, or system error), the step fails and the job stops, leaving Card Number-based Transaction lookup unavailable to both online CICS users and batch programs

rules.Rule_Name: STEP25 - IDCAMS - Define Card Number Transaction Lookup Access Path
rules.Rule_Description: This step creates a named logical access path called AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX.PATH that serves as the stable, application-facing entry point for retrieving Card Transaction records by Card Number. The path is permanently linked to the Card Number Alternate Index (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX), enabling CardDemo application programs to look up all transactions associated with a specific Credit Card without needing to reference the underlying index structure directly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Primary Dataset (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS) has been successfully created and populated with all initial daily Transaction records, AND the Card Number Alternate Index structure (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX) has been defined with Card Number (26 bytes at byte position 304 of each 350-byte Transaction record) as the secondary lookup key, AND the Alternate Index is currently empty (no index entries exist yet)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The BLDINDEX process is executed reading every Transaction record sequentially from the Transaction Primary Dataset (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS) and writing all resulting Card Number-to-Transaction-ID mappings into the Card Number Alternate Index (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card Number Alternate Index must be fully populated with an index entry for every unique Card Number found across all Transaction records, AND each Card Number index entry must reference ALL Transaction IDs that share that same Card Number (reflecting the one-card-to-many-transactions business relationship), AND upon successful completion, CardDemo application programs must be able to retrieve all Transaction records belonging to a specific Credit Card Number by opening the Card Number Access Path (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.VSAM.AIX.PATH), AND if the BLDINDEX process fails for any reason (e.g., source dataset unavailable, target index structure missing, or insufficient disk space), the Card Number Alternate Index remains empty and all Card Number-based Transaction lookup functions return no data, causing the step and job to fail

rules.Rule_Name: STEP30 - IDCAMS BLDINDEX - Build Card Number Alternate Index from Transaction Records
rules.Rule_Description: After the Transaction Primary Dataset has been loaded with all daily Transaction records, this step scans every Transaction record and builds the Card Number Alternate Index. This enables CardDemo application programs to retrieve all transactions associated with a specific Credit Card Number using the pre-defined Card Number Access Path.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Master File batch rebuild process (dataset deletion, creation, data load, alternate index definition, path definition, and index build) has fully completed, AND the TRANSACT file in CICS region CICSAWSA is currently in a CLOSED state from the pre-processing step
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The OPCIFIL step executes and issues the CEMT SET FILE command targeting the TRANSACT file in CICS region CICSAWSA with the OPEN directive
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The TRANSACT file in CICS region CICSAWSA is set to OPEN status, restoring online user access to Transaction records via Transaction ID-based lookup and posting through CICS application screens

rules.Rule_Name: OPCIFIL - SDSF/CEMT - Restore Online Transaction File Access After Batch Rebuild
rules.Rule_Description: After the Transaction Master File batch rebuild is fully completed, the TRANSACT file in the CICS online region CICSAWSA must be reopened so that online users can resume Transaction ID-based inquiries and postings.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Master File batch rebuild process (including the Card Number Alternate Index build in STEP30) has fully completed, AND the CXACAIX file in CICS region CICSAWSA is currently in a CLOSED state from the pre-processing step
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The OPCIFIL step executes and issues the CEMT SET FILE command targeting the CXACAIX file in CICS region CICSAWSA with the OPEN directive
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The CXACAIX file in CICS region CICSAWSA is set to OPEN status, restoring online user access to Card Number-based Transaction history lookups — enabling retrieval of all transactions associated with a specific Credit Card Number through CICS application screens

rules.Rule_Name: OPCIFIL - SDSF/CEMT - Restore Online Card Number Transaction Lookup Access After Batch Rebuild
rules.Rule_Description: After the Transaction Master File batch rebuild is fully completed, the CXACAIX file (Card Number Alternate Index path) in the CICS online region CICSAWSA must be reopened so that online users can resume Card Number-based Transaction history inquiries.
